questions.explain: 'Gesund' means 'healthy'; the opposite is 'ungesund' (unhealthy).

questions.q: Which sentence means 'There is no cinema in my village'?
options: In meiner Stadt gibt es ein Kino
In meinem Dorf gibt es ein Kino
In meinem Dorf gibt es kein Kino
questions.explain: 'Das Dorf' = 'village', 'kein Kino' = 'no cinema', 'es gibt' = 'there is'.
'Der Nachbar' means 'the neighbour' (female: 'die Nachbarin').

questions.q: What does 'Der Zug hat Verspätung' mean?
questions.explain: 'Verspätung haben' means 'to be delayed/late', so 'Der Zug hat Verspätung' = 'The train is delayed'.
'In der Nähe' means 'nearby/close by', e.g. 'in der Nähe der Schule' = 'near the school'.
'Die Fahrkarte' is a travel 'ticket'; 'die Landkarte' = map, 'der Führerschein' = driving licence.
'Zuverlässig' means 'reliable/dependable' (related to 'sich verlassen auf').

questions.q: What does 'Ich wohne am Stadtrand' mean?
options: I live on the outskirts of town
I live in the city centre
questions.explain: 'Der Stadtrand' means 'the edge/outskirts of the town', so 'Ich wohne am Stadtrand' = 'I live on the outskirts'.

questions.q: How do you say 'My house has a large garden'?
options: Meine Wohnung hat einen großen Garten
Mein Haus hat einen großen Garten
Mein Haus hat einen kleinen Garten
questions.explain: 'Einen großen Garten' = 'a large garden'; 'kleinen' (small) is the distractor.

questions.q: Which sentence means 'You must avoid fatty food'?
questions.explain: 'Man muss' = 'one must' and 'vermeiden' = 'to avoid', so this means 'You must avoid fatty food'.
'Malen' means 'to paint'; don't confuse with 'mahlen' (to grind).
'Verreisen' means 'to go away/travel (somewhere)'.

questions.q: Which sentence means 'Next year I will travel to Austria' (future)?
options: Letztes Jahr bin ich nach Österreich gereist
Nächstes Jahr werde ich nach Österreich reisen
questions.explain: 'Werde... reisen' is the future tense 'will travel'; with 'nächstes Jahr' (next year) the future is correct.

options: The crew of a ship only
questions.explain: 'Die Mannschaft' means 'the team', e.g. 'die Fußballmannschaft' = 'the football team'.
'Das Wohlbefinden' means 'wellbeing'. ('Die Wohnung' = flat — a near-miss distractor.)
'Der Flug' means 'the flight'; 'fliegen' = 'to fly'. ('Der Fluss' = river is the near-miss.)
False friend: 'die Note' is a school 'grade/mark' (e.g. 'eine gute Note'), not an English 'note'.
'Großzügig' means 'generous'; it does not literally mean 'big' despite containing 'groß'.
'Die Einwohner' means 'the inhabitants/residents' of a place.

questions.q: How do you say 'He has curly brown hair'?
questions.explain: 'Lockig' = 'curly' and 'braune Haare' = 'brown hair'; 'glatt' (straight) is the distractor.

questions.q: How do you say 'My town is too noisy'?
questions.explain: 'Laut' means 'loud/noisy'; 'ruhig' (quiet) is the opposite distractor.
'Die Mahlzeit' means 'the meal'.
